title: Entanglement assisted quantum $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes
authors: Carlos Galindo, Fernando Hernando, Helena Martín-Cruz, Ryutaroh Matsumoto
abstract: Quantum $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes are quantum error-correcting codes capable of correcting $δ-1$ qudit erasures within one subset of qudits of cardinality at most $r+δ-1$. In this paper, we introduce the more general framework of entanglement-assisted quantum $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes, assuming that the local recovery operation is assisted by receiver-held qudits that remain unaffected by erasures.   We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to satisfy this property. For codes derived from Hermitian or Euclidean constructions, we establish connections between entanglement-assisted quantum and classical notions of $(r,δ)$-local recoverability, and derive a Singleton-like bound. Furthermore, we construct optimal pure entan\-gle\-ment-assisted quantum $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes from several families of classical codes, including bivariate $J$-affine variety codes, BCH codes, and homothetic-BCH codes.
summary: This paper introduces the framework for entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes, generalizing existing quantum error-correcting codes. It derives necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes and constructs optimal examples using established classical code families. This advances the theoretical understanding of quantum information protection against localized erasures.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop and characterize entanglement-assisted quantum $(r, \delta)$-locally recoverable codes (EA $(r, \delta)$-QLRCs).
main_result: The authors establish necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes and construct optimal pure EA $(r, \delta)$-QLRCs using known classical code families like BCH and J-affine variety codes.
method: The methodology involves establishing theoretical bounds, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions based on algebraic structures (Euclidean/Hermitian inner products), and providing explicit constructions parameterized by classical code properties.
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs) designed to protect quantum states from local erasures, generalized by incorporating entanglement assistance via receiver-held qudits.
key_observables: Code parameters like $[[n, k, d; c]]_q$, and the locality parameters $(r, \delta)$ defining the error correction capability.
important_parameters: The locality parameters $(r, \delta)$, the number of entangled pairs ($c$), and the underlying finite field structure ($\mathbb{F}_q$).
main_assumptions: The local recovery operation is assumed to be assisted by receiver-held qudits that remain unaffected by erasures.
paper_structure: The paper builds from background material on classical and quantum LRCs, formalizes the EA $(r, \delta)$-QLRC framework, derives necessary and sufficient conditions, and concludes with explicit constructions of optimal codes from various classical code families.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools for quantum information security, directly relevant to designing robust quantum communication channels against localized noise.
